paragraphs.text: I met my old swimming teacher outside the hardware shop. We talked about the pool closing and about her move to a smaller flat. The afternoon unfolded into one of those stretches when things happen and life carries itself onward. By the time I reached home, the bread I had bought was cold.

The regent dismissed the council and appointed her nephew to oversee the granaries. What followed was a season of developments, with circumstances gathering pace and events taking their course. A surviving letter from the western province complains that the new overseer demanded payment before releasing grain to the garrison.

My first week in the coastal town began with a broken suitcase wheel and a room above a fish shop. After that, days filled themselves with the ongoing business of being days, each bringing its share of whatever came along. On Friday I bought a bicycle from the shopkeeper's nephew.

The three transfers blurred together in my memory, but the ticket stubs reconstruct the journey. We left the ferry at 10:15, boarded the inland coach at 10:40, and changed to the village minibus at noon. That last change explains why the through ticket was cheaper than the route advertised at the harbor.

The apprentice had finished tightening the vise when the foreman entered. What followed was a blur of events, each event arriving as part of what was happening, until the events had happened. An hour later, a signed warning lay on the bench beside the apprentice's lunch tin and the unfinished brass fitting.

At the station, the porter told us the branch train had been canceled and pointed toward a row of buses. Everything after that became a wash of motion, the motion of things moving as movement filled the interval. By evening we were seated in a restaurant forty miles from the hotel we had booked.

The laboratory's maintenance log calls the morning a blur because its wall clock stopped during a power cut. Instrument timestamps still establish the sequence: the freezer alarm preceded the restart, and the sample transfer followed it. The reconstruction explains the uncertainty in staff recollections and preserves the order needed to assess the interruption.
The instructor tapped the rim of a cup to bring everyone back from the corridor. Everything after the bell was a fog. I found my coat beneath the bench and waited by the gate for the minibus.

Everything after the bell was a blur in the film: condensation covered the camera's protective window during the outdoor procession. The editor retained the clear opening shot and replaced the obscured footage with still photographs taken from the sheltered balcony.

The rest of the morning was a blur because the anaesthetic left the fictional narrator unable to retain new memories until lunch. Her sister's notes record the journey home and the pharmacy stop that she later could not recall.
